overview: The paper proposes Self-adaptive Schema Scaffolding (S3), a training-free method that enables diffusion large language models (dLLMs) to generate reliable structured outputs by injecting compiled schema templates with mask tokens as initial denoising states, combined with a top-K remasking strategy and null-token-based adaptive length management, evaluated across structural adherence, content fidelity, and faithfulness dimensions.

modules.name: Schema Compiler
modules.description: Parses structural specifications (JSON schema, XML XSD, etc.) and compiles them into scaffold templates by identifying invariant structural tokens (brackets, delimiters, field names) and replacing variable content positions with mask tokens. Supports multiple output formats (JSON, XML, YAML) via pluggable parser modules.

modules.name: Self-Adaptive Scaffold Generator
modules.description: Extends the compiled scaffold with adaptive null-token placeholders for variable-length and optional fields. Incorporates augmented prompt construction (Q+) that instructs the model to use null tokens for absent values, transforming fixed-length scaffolding into an adaptive generation task without requiring fine-tuning.

modules.name: Diffusion Model Wrapper
modules.description: Abstract interface for dLLM backends (LLaDA, Dream-7B) that handles model loading, conditional generation with fixed instruction prefix concatenation, single-step denoising factorization, and confidence score extraction for masked positions. Manages context composition of instruction Q and scaffold A_s.

modules.name: Top-K Remasking Strategy
modules.description: Implements the iterative denoising loop with deterministic top-K remasking where K equals total masked tokens divided by number of denoising steps. At each iteration, predicts all masked positions, keeps the highest-confidence tokens, and re-masks the lowest-confidence K tokens for refinement in subsequent steps.

modules.name: Alternative Remasking Strategies
modules.description: Implements baseline remasking approaches for ablation comparison: Low-Confidence remasking (selectively discards tokens below entropy/log-probability thresholds) and Block-wise remasking (sliding-window semi-autoregressive mechanism with configurable block size).

modules.name: Data Preprocessing Pipeline
modules.description: Processes structured output datasets (WikiBio, MBPP, MultiWOZ, FUNSD) by extracting source documents and corresponding structured targets, tokenizing with the dLLM's tokenizer, and aligning inputs with their structural specifications. Handles format-specific preprocessing for biography generation, code generation, dialogue state tracking, and form filling tasks.

modules.name: Baseline Prompt Construction
modules.description: Constructs detailed instruction prompts for baseline methods including direct prompting (with full JSON schema in instruction), few-shot prompting (with in-context examples), and template-as-guidance prompting (with complete schema description as textual guidance). Generates the corresponding fully-masked initial states for standard dLLM inference.

modules.name: Evaluation: Structural Adherence
modules.description: Computes three structural metrics: Structure Validity (proportion of syntactically valid and parseable outputs), Field Completeness (percentage of required fields correctly populated), and Schema Compliance (strictest metric checking data types, value constraints, and nested structures). Validates against the predefined schema specification.

modules.name: Evaluation: Content Fidelity
modules.description: Computes field-level precision, recall, and F1 scores comparing generated content against ground truth. Supports both exact match and fuzzy match strategies to accommodate minor textual variations preserving semantic meaning. Performs per-field-type analysis for detailed behavioral assessment across content categories.

modules.name: Evaluation: Faithfulness and Hallucination
modules.description: Computes Hallucination Rate by measuring the proportion of output fields containing information not present in or not reasonably inferable from the source text. Implements source-grounded verification logic that cross-references generated field values against the original document content.

modules.name: Denoising Step Sweep Experiment
modules.description: Orchestrates experiments across varying denoising step counts (8, 16, 32) for all methods (baseline, S2, S3) to analyze the trade-off between computational budget and output quality. Captures the overthinking phenomenon where extended iteration degrades content fidelity.

modules.name: Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Manages controlled ablation experiments comparing baseline, few-shot, template-as-guidance, vanilla schema scaffolding (S2), and self-adaptive schema scaffolding (S3) under identical conditions. Isolates the contribution of each component (scaffolding, null tokens, remasking strategy) by incremental enhancement.

modules.name: Cross-Domain and Cross-Architecture Validation
modules.description: Runs evaluation on diverse structural output tasks (code generation on MBPP, dialogue state tracking on MultiWOZ, form filling on FUNSD) and different dLLM architectures (LLaDA, Dream-7B) to validate generalizability. Applies identical S3 hyperparameters across all settings without task-specific tuning.

modules.name: Computational Complexity Analyzer
modules.description: Profiles inference latency, memory usage, and computational cost across methods and denoising step configurations. Calculates asymptotic complexity comparisons between standard dLLM (O(L^3) for full reverse process) and S3 (O(nL^2) with warm-start initialization) and measures actual wall-clock speedups.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration and Reporting
modules.description: Manages YAML/JSON-based experiment configurations with inheritance for method variants and hyperparameter sweeps. Aggregates results across all evaluation dimensions, generates LaTeX tables matching paper format (Tables 1-5), produces denoising-step-vs-metric plots (Figures 3-4), and tracks experiment provenance for reproducibility.
